Outside rung (24 Oct 21:20 CT): on the 56 sampled current-template degruyterbrill.com pages where the parser reads <contributor-popdown affiliations=...>, 152 of 152 author affiliations match the publisher's own Crossref deposit for the same author position (token overlap >= 0.6; oxjob #1808 work/crossref_aff_check.py). evidence: oxjob #2146 (physics societies, 10 Nov 2026): IOP Publishing shows author e-mails only for corresponding authors, so a single listed author e-mail is IOP's corresponding mark. Evidence: on IOP's author-card template (dt.author-list__name), where both an author's e-mail and the 'Author(s) to whom any correspondence should be addressed' note are visible, the authors with an e-mail are exactly the noted authors on 9 of 10 sampled pages (10th: one extra e-mail); #2146 work/iop_email_test.py over 800 seeded stored pages. The gold already marks the author-card e-mail as corresponding on 2053-1591/ab278d and 0022-3727/49/36/364002. This page lists one author e-mail, matching C. Borcea in the separate 'Author e-mails' block (borcea@nipne.ro). Label-v1's exclusion is an e-mail 'shown for every author'; here one author of 3 has one. Ruling affects ~250K IOP works that show this flag today.
ruling: upheld (16 Nov 2026, #1791): gold v1.5. Follows charter § 6 2026-11-10 20:40 (#2146): IOP shows author e-mails only for corresponding authors, so an e-mail the page shows for some authors but not all (an author card's EMAIL entry or the 'Author e-mails' block, tied to the author by card or by name) marks that author. label-v1's exclusion stays: an e-mail shown for every author is not a mark (dev 2cf002e4 keeps none). Every IOP page in dev (20 with e-mails) and holdout read by #1791: 8 dev cells move (these 4 + 54022cc8, cad8d1ef, 6d526bb8, 769bfab1), 4 holdout. Two holdout pages print IOP's 'to whom any correspondence' note with no author carrying its marker: they keep none.
